findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant work
findings.body: After taking the RLock and finding entryPointAssetsCache == nil, the code unconditionally acquires the write lock and recomputes the assets without re-checking whether another goroutine already populated the cache while waiting for the lock. If multiple goroutines call GetWebAssets concurrently on a cold cache (e.g. right after startup), each one that was blocked on entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() will redundantly re-read the manifest file (or hit the CDN) and overwrite entryPointAssetsCache again, instead of returning the value the first goroutine just computed. This does not reintroduce the data race, but it defeats part of the purpose of caching and can cause unnecessary file/network I/O under concurrent load.

findings.title: No regression test added for the fixed data race
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the entryPointAssetsCache global by adding a mutex, but no test (e.g. a -race enabled test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently from multiple goroutines) was added to verify the fix or to prevent regressions if the locking is refactored later. Without such a test, a future change could silently reintroduce the race without being caught by CI.
